get.summary:
Lists dashboards under a parent. The parent may be an organization
(returns the system-curated catalog) or a space (returns
user-managed dashboards).
get.description:
The `dashboards.read` permission gates the verb regardless of
parent scope; the membership interceptor ahead of it enforces
org-membership at org parent and space-membership at space parent.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Optional. Maximum number of dashboards to return.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: Optional. Page token from a previous ListDashboards call.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Optional. An expression for filtering the results of the request.
Filter rules are case insensitive. Filterable fields:

+ `displayName`
+ `createTime` (supports comparison operators)

Examples:

+ `displayName = "Overview"` — exact match on display name.
+ `createTime > "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"` — created after date.

For more information, see [AIP-160](https://aip.dev/160).

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description:
Optional. A comma-separated list of fields to order by. The default
order is ascending. Use "desc" after a field name for descending.
Supported fields:

+ `displayName`
+ `createTime`

Example: `createTime desc, displayName`

If not specified, the results are ordered by `createTime` descending.

AxisConfigScale.description:
Axis scale types.

 - SCALE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified; defaults to LINEAR.
 - LINEAR: Linear scale.
 - LOG10: Logarithmic (base 10) scale.

ChartWidgetChartType.description:
Chart visualization types.

 - CHART_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified chart type; defaults to LINE.
 - LINE: Line chart.
 - BAR: Bar chart.
 - AREA: Area chart.
 - STACKED_BAR: Stacked bar chart.
 - STACKED_AREA: Stacked area chart.
 - SCATTER: Scatter plot.

CollectionWidgetDisplayMode.description:
How the rows are visually arranged. The renderer picks layout
primitives per mode (e.g. `Table` for TABLE, a card grid for CARD).

 - DISPLAY_MODE_UNSPECIFIED: Default; the renderer picks based on `supported_modes` (first
entry) or falls back to TABLE.
 - TABLE: Classic tabular rendering with sortable columns.
 - CARD: Card-grid rendering — each row becomes a card with thumbnail.

DashboardManagementMode.description:
Identifies who owns the lifecycle of a dashboard. SYSTEM_MANAGED
dashboards are server-curated and reject all mutations; USER_MANAGED
dashboards are owned by the customer and support full CRUD.

 - MANAGEMENT_MODE_UNSPECIFIED: Default. Server handlers always populate this field on read,
so UNSPECIFIED on the wire indicates a server bug, not a
legitimate state.
 - USER_MANAGED: Customer-owned. Full CRUD applies.
 - SYSTEM_MANAGED: Server-curated. Mutations are rejected with FAILED_PRECONDITION.

IconConfigIconSize.description:
Display size hint for the leading icon. The renderer maps each
bucket to a platform-appropriate point size.

 - ICON_SIZE_UNSPECIFIED: Default; renderer picks a context-appropriate size.
 - SMALL: Compact size — typical for inline list rows.
 - MEDIUM: Default mid-size — typical for card thumbnails.
 - LARGE: Larger thumbnail emphasis.
 - EXTRA_LARGE: Hero-size thumbnail; used for empty-state and primary tiles.

PieChartWidgetPieChartType.description:
Pie chart visualization types.

 - PIE_CHART_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified; defaults to PIE.
 - PIE: Standard pie chart.
 - DONUT: Donut chart.

TextWidgetFormat.description:
Text format types.

 - FORMAT_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified; defaults to MARKDOWN.
 - MARKDOWN: Markdown-formatted text.
 - PLAIN_TEXT: Plain text.

ThresholdDirection.description:
Direction relative to the threshold value.

 - DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified direction.
 - ABOVE: Values above the threshold.
 - BELOW: Values below the threshold.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

code.description:
The status code, which should be an enum value of
[google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description:
A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any
user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the
[google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized
by the client.

details.description:
A list of messages that carry the error details.  There is a common set of
message types for APIs to use.

rpcStatus.description:
The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for
different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is
used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains
three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details.

You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the
[API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

red.description: The amount of red in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].

green.description: The amount of green in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].

blue.description: The amount of blue in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].

alpha.description:
`pixel color = alpha * (this color) + (1.0 - alpha) * (background color)`

This means that a value of 1.0 corresponds to a solid color, whereas
a value of 0.0 corresponds to a completely transparent color. This
uses a wrapper message rather than a simple float scalar so that it is
possible to distinguish between a default value and the value being unset.
If omitted, this color object is rendered as a solid color
(as if the alpha value had been explicitly given a value of 1.0).

The fraction of this color that should be applied to the pixel. That is,

startTime.description: Required. The start of the time range.

endTime.description: Required. The end of the time range.

v1AbsoluteTimeRange.description: AbsoluteTimeRange defines an explicit start and end time.

v1Aggregation.description:
Aggregation functions that can be applied to resource queries.

 - AGGREGATION_UNSPECIFIED: No aggregation specified.
 - AGGREGATION_COUNT: Count of matching resources.
 - AGGREGATION_SUM: Sum of the aggregation field.
 - AGGREGATION_AVG: Average of the aggregation field.
 - AGGREGATION_MIN: Minimum value of the aggregation field.
 - AGGREGATION_MAX: Maximum value of the aggregation field.

v1AxisConfig.description: AxisConfig defines display properties for a chart axis.

dataSource.description: Required. The data source for this series.

label.description: Optional. The display label for this series.

color.description: Optional. The color for this series.

v1ChartDataSet.description: ChartDataSet is a single data series within a ChartWidget.

dataSets.description: Required. The data sets to plot. Each data set becomes a series.

thresholds.description: Optional. Threshold lines drawn on the chart.

v1ChartWidget.description: ChartWidget displays time series or categorical data as an XY chart.

dataSource.description: Required. The data source for collection rows.

columns.description: Optional. Column definitions. If empty, columns are auto-detected.

rowsPerPage.description: Optional. Number of rows per page. Defaults to server-chosen value.

displayMode.description:
Optional. The current display mode for the widget. If unset, the
renderer treats this as DISPLAY_MODE_UNSPECIFIED and picks based
on `supported_modes`.

supportedModes.description:
Optional. Modes the customer can switch between via the safe-edit
UI. If empty, the widget is locked to `display_mode`. Modes not
listed are not user-selectable even if the renderer can render
them.

Mode-selection matrix (worked examples):

  display_mode=UNSPECIFIED, supported_modes=[]
    → renderer picks TABLE (single mode, no toggle UI).

  display_mode=UNSPECIFIED, supported_modes=[CARD, TABLE]
    → renderer picks CARD (first listed); user can toggle to TABLE.

  display_mode=CARD, supported_modes=[]
    → locked to CARD; user cannot toggle.

  display_mode=TABLE, supported_modes=[CARD, TABLE]
    → starts at TABLE; user can toggle between TABLE and CARD.

rowActions.description:
Optional. Per-row actions exposed by the renderer (e.g. "open",
"share", "archive"). Populated by the server template per resource
type.

iconConfig.description: Optional. How to derive each row's leading icon / thumbnail.

emptyState.description: Optional. Content displayed when the data source returns no rows.

v1CollectionWidget.description:
CollectionWidget displays a collection of rows in one of several
display modes (table, card grid). The same data source feeds every
mode; switching modes is a presentation concern handled by the
client renderer.

Naming note: the widget is mode-agnostic by design. New display
modes (e.g. a vertical list with leading icon and trailing detail)
get added to `DisplayMode` only when a concrete consumer plus a
renderer implementation land in the same change. Shipping an enum
value the renderer can't handle creates a silent downgrade; don't.

field.description: Required. The field name from the data source.

displayName.description: Optional. The display name for the column header.

visible.description: Optional. Whether this column is visible. Defaults to true.

sortable.description: Optional. Whether the customer can sort by this column.

filterable.description:
Optional. Whether the customer can filter on this column. May be
combined with `visible = false` to expose a filterable-but-hidden
field.

v1Column.description:
Column defines a column in a CollectionWidget. The same column set
describes the data shape across every display mode (TABLE, CARD,
…) — TABLE renders columns as headers, CARD picks the marked
columns to surface on the card face, and so on.

A column may participate in user-driven sorting and filtering even
if it is not visually rendered: a column with `visible = false,
filterable = true` exposes a filterable field that the customer can
query without the column ever appearing in TABLE mode.

v1Dashboard.description: A dashboard at the organization or space scope.

displayName.description: Optional. A human-readable label for the variable.

defaultValue.description: Optional. The default value when no selection is made.

allowedValues.description: Optional. A fixed set of allowed values. If empty, any value is accepted.

v1DashboardVariable.description: A template variable that can be referenced in widget queries.

v1DataSource.description:
DataSource defines where a widget gets its data. Extensible via the `source`
oneof — new source types (SQL, external APIs) can be added later.

title.description: Optional. Headline shown above the subtitle.

subtitle.description: Optional. Secondary line of explanatory copy.

icon.description: Optional. Cross-platform semantic icon shown above the title.

primaryAction.description:
Optional. The primary call-to-action presented in the empty state
(e.g. an "Upload" or "Invite" button).

v1EmptyState.description:
EmptyState is shown when a CollectionWidget's data source returns
zero rows. It is purely presentational — the renderer composes the
title, subtitle, icon, and primary action.

columns.description: Optional. The number of columns in the grid. Defaults to 12 if unset.

tiles.description: Optional. The tiles arranged on the grid.

v1GridLayout.description: GridLayout positions tiles on a column-based grid. Maps to react-grid-layout.

v1Icon.description:
Icon is a curated cross-platform semantic icon catalog. Renderers map
each value to a platform-native icon (SF Symbols on macOS, Fluent
System Icons on Windows, equivalent on the web). The enum is purely
semantic — variants like filled vs. outlined are chosen by the
renderer based on context.

Numeric values are partitioned into thousand-blocks per category.
Within a category, values are sequential: enum numbers are wire
identifiers, not display order, so middle-of-category alphabetical
insertion isn't an invariant. Pre-prod freedom permits reordering
the source list (and renumbering) until the first paying customer
persists a row that references one of these values.

New icons must be added in three places at once: this enum, the
macOS SF Symbol map, and the WinUI Fluent map. CI lint catches
drift.

Categories (thousand-block ranges):

  * File / content types   — 1xxx
  * Identity               — 2xxx
  * Actions                — 3xxx
  * Status                 — 4xxx
  * Navigation             — 5xxx

 - ICON_UNSPECIFIED: Default value when no icon is specified. Renderers may pick an
appropriate fallback.
 - ICON_DOCUMENT: Generic document. (File / content types.)
 - ICON_FOLDER: A folder or container.
 - ICON_PHOTO: A photograph or raster image.
 - ICON_VIDEO: A video clip.
 - ICON_AUDIO: An audio clip.
 - ICON_CODE: Source code or a code snippet.
 - ICON_ARCHIVE: An archive (zip, tar, etc.).
 - ICON_PERSON: A single person / individual user. (Identity.)
 - ICON_PEOPLE: A group of people.
 - ICON_ORGANIZATION: An organization, company, or team.
 - ICON_SHARE: Share an item. (Actions.)
 - ICON_TRASH: Move to trash / delete.
 - ICON_TAG: A tag / label.
 - ICON_PIN: Pin an item to a position.
 - ICON_STAR: Mark an item as starred / favorite.
 - ICON_DOWNLOAD: Download an item.
 - ICON_UPLOAD: Upload an item.
 - ICON_COPY: Copy / duplicate an item.
 - ICON_EDIT: Edit / modify an item.
 - ICON_CHECK: Success / completed indicator. (Status.)
 - ICON_X_MARK: Close / dismiss / failure indicator.
 - ICON_WARNING: Warning indicator.
 - ICON_INFO: Informational indicator.
 - ICON_LOCK: Locked state.
 - ICON_UNLOCKED: Unlocked state.
 - ICON_ELLIPSIS: Overflow / "more options" indicator (typically `…`). (Navigation.)
 - ICON_PLUS: Add / create.
 - ICON_MINUS: Remove / subtract.
 - ICON_SETTINGS: Settings / configuration.
 - ICON_SEARCH: Search.

sourceField.description:
Optional. Name of the row field whose value is a thumbnail URL.
When set and non-empty, the renderer fetches the image (subject to
gateway-host bearer-token attachment).

iconField.description:
Optional. Name of the row field whose value is the numeric
`Icon` enum value (e.g. `1002` for `ICON_PHOTO`). Encoded as the
wire integer rather than the symbolic name so renaming an `Icon`
value never silently breaks persisted dashboards. Server handlers
synthesize this per row.

initialsField.description:
Optional. Name of the row field whose value is used to derive
initials when no thumbnail or semantic icon is available
(typically "display_name" or "name").

fallbackIcon.description:
Optional. The static fallback icon used when none of
`source_field` / `icon_field` / `initials_field` produces a value.

size.description:
Optional. The size hint for the leading icon — applies to whichever
derivation path resolved.

fallbackColor.description:
Optional. Background color for the icon backplate. Renderer-honored
when icon or initials are shown without a thumbnail.

v1IconConfig.description:
IconConfig describes how to derive the leading icon / thumbnail for
each row in a CollectionWidget. The four derivation paths
(`source_field` → `icon_field` → `initials_field` → `fallback_icon`)
are tried in order: the first one that produces a value wins.
`size` and `fallback_color` are presentation knobs that apply to
whichever derivation path resolves.

nextPageToken.description: Token for the next page of results.

dataSource.description: Required. The data source for the chart segments.

pieChartType.description: Optional. The pie chart visualization type.

showLabels.description: Optional. Whether to display labels on segments.

showLegend.description: Optional. Whether to display a legend.

v1PieChartWidget.description: PieChartWidget displays data as a pie or donut chart.

duration.description: Required. The duration of the time range, measured backwards from now.

v1RelativeTimeRange.description: RelativeTimeRange defines a time window relative to the current time.

resourceType.description:
Required. The fully-qualified Pivox resource type to query
(e.g. "pivox.api/Proxy").

filter.description: Optional. An AIP-160 filter expression applied to the resources.

aggregation.description: Optional. The aggregation function to apply.

aggregationField.description:
Optional. The field to aggregate on. Required when aggregation is
SUM, AVG, MIN, or MAX.

groupingFields.description: Optional. Fields to group results on.

timeRange.description: Optional. The time range for the query.

timeGranularity.description: Optional. The granularity for time-series bucketing.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum number of results to return.

v1ResourceQuery.description:
ResourceQuery describes a query against Pivox resources. It is a declarative
DSL stored in the dashboard configuration; a future QueryDashboardData RPC
will resolve it server-side.

key.description:
Required. Well-known action key. Maps client-side to the actual
behavior. Examples: "open_detail", "share", "archive", "delete".

The pattern constraint keeps keys safe to use as renderer
dispatch-table keys and prevents typos like "Open Detail" leaking
into wire data.

label.description: Optional. The display label shown in menus / buttons.

icon.description: Optional. Cross-platform semantic icon for this action.

requiresConfirmation.description:
Optional. If true, the renderer presents a confirmation prompt
before executing this action.

v1RowAction.description:
RowAction describes an action exposed on each row of a
CollectionWidget. The `key` is a well-known string the renderer
maps to a platform UI behavior (e.g. "open_detail" → push detail
sheet, "share" → present share dialog). The renderer owns the
dispatch table; the server only declares which actions are
available.

subtitle.description: Optional. A subtitle displayed below the widget title.

dividerBelow.description: Optional. Whether to render a divider line below the header.

v1SectionHeader.description: SectionHeader is a visual separator for organizing dashboard sections.

v1StaticData.description: StaticData provides hardcoded data points for a widget.

label.description: Required. The label for this data point.

value.description: Required. The numeric value of this data point.

v1StaticDataPoint.description: StaticDataPoint is a single labeled numeric value.

dataSource.description: Required. The data source for the statistic value.

thresholds.description: Optional. Thresholds for color-coding the value.

sparkline.description: Optional. Whether to show a sparkline trend below the value.

v1StatisticWidget.description: StatisticWidget displays a single KPI value with optional sparkline.

v1TextWidget.description: TextWidget displays rich text or markdown content.

color.description: Optional. The color to use when the threshold is triggered.

direction.description: Optional. The direction relative to the threshold value.

label.description: Optional. A human-readable label for the threshold.

v1Threshold.description: Threshold defines a value boundary for color-coding or reference lines.

xPos.description: Required. The zero-indexed column position of the tile.

yPos.description: Required. The zero-indexed row position of the tile.

width.description: Required. The width of the tile in columns. Must be at least 1.

height.description: Required. The height of the tile in rows. Must be at least 1.

widget.description: Required. The widget displayed in this tile.

v1Tile.description: Tile represents a positioned widget within a GridLayout.

absolute.description: An absolute time range with explicit start and end.

v1TimeRange.description: TimeRange specifies the time window for a query.

id.description: Optional. Client-assigned identifier for the widget.

title.description: Optional. The display title of the widget.

chart.description: An XY chart (line, bar, area, etc.).

collection.description:
A collection of resources rendered in one of several display
modes (table, card grid, …).

v1Widget.description: Widget contains a single dashboard component.
